newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower as export lineup dwindles.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower as export lineup dwindles.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on scant exports, fund selling and increased export competition from overseas contenders, traders said.
"Export demand is very poor, especially on wheat," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
"They're guessing the numbers (USDA weekly exports) will be low tomorrow," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
The fund selling was led by Lee B. Stern and Co's sale of four million bushels of December near midday which drove the market to the session lows, traders said.
Prices were knocked to contract lows by the bearish exports. The new low for March is $3.99-1/2 per bushel, down from the previous low of $4.02 set October 4.

Algeria this week bought 100,000 tonnes of wheat from France rather than the United States, Jordan Thursday bought 150,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina, Australia and Canada and there are signs the European Union remains poised to hike rebates for its export wheat.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,500 contracts, down from 15,190 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat futures closed 3-3/4 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 6-1/4 at $4.11.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, up from 5,554 Wednesday.
